rationale: Electrophysiological, genetic, and imaging studies consistently support the classification of FDXR-associated auditory neuropathy spectrum disorder (ANSD) as post-synaptic rather than pre-synaptic, characterized by severe cochlear nerve atrophy, mitochondrial dysfunction in auditory neurons, and altered electrically evoked compound action potentials (ECAP). However, literature is divided on cochlear implant (CI) outcomes and efficacy. While individual cohort studies and reports report marked postoperative improvements and favorable rehabilitation when CI stimulation parameters (such as pulse width or rate) are modified, broader comparative cohort investigations report that post-synaptic ANSD cases generally exhibit limited ECAP responses, significantly smaller functional and electrophysiological gains than pre-synaptic ANSD cases, and potential long-term deterioration due to progressive retrocochlear degeneration.

evidence.text: Post-lingual postsynaptic ANSD, including cases with novel FDXR mutations, showed significantly greater cochlear nerve atrophy than presynaptic ANSD and simple sensorineural hearing loss. However, speech scores markedly improved after cochlear implantation without correlation to nerve size.

source.title: Cochlear nerve atrophy in postlingual ANSD: diagnostic clue and implications for cochlear implantation
source.quote: Postsynaptic post-ANSD showed significantly greater CN atrophy than presynaptic cases and sSNHL. Although CN atrophy was pronounced, it did not predict poor CI outcomes within the observed thresholds. Speech scores improved markedly post-CI, with no correlation to CN size.

evidence.text: A hearing-impaired patient with co-segregation of FDXR variants displaying post-synaptic ANSD via mitochondrial dysfunction underwent cochlear implantation with favorable outcomes after mapping pulse width adjustments.

conflicts: While single-case and selective post-lingual ANSD studies report substantial speech score improvements post-CI despite severe cochlear nerve atrophy when pulse widths are adjusted, systematic multi-patient cohort trials show that post-synaptic ANSD patients achieve significantly lower functional gains (CAP/SIR scores) and poorer ECAP responses than pre-synaptic ANSD patients.

Longitudinal follow-ups in mitochondrial-associated auditory neuropathies indicate a risk of secondary speech perception decline over time caused by ongoing progressive retrocochlear degeneration, contradicting assumptions of uniformly stable or uniquely efficacious long-term CI outcomes.

new_directions.question_text: Does systematically increasing pulse width or lowering stimulation rate rescue speech recognition performance specifically in FDXR-associated ANSD compared to conventional CI mapping strategies?
new_directions.rationale: Single-case mapping adjustments have shown positive functional responses, but controlled trials across post-synaptic mitochondrial neuropathies have yet to evaluate whether extended pulse widths specifically overcome the neural transmission deficits of FDXR deficiency.

new_directions.question_text: What is the rate of retrocochlear auditory degradation over 5 to 10 years in FDXR-variant patients following cochlear implantation?
new_directions.rationale: Given evidence of late speech degradation in mitochondrial retrocochlear neuropathies, longitudinal auditory profiling is required to determine whether CI benefit persists or deteriorates as systemic mitochondrial dysfunction advances.
